metadata.name: [GCP GKE OTel] Container memory near limit
metadata.description: Fires for each container whose non-evictable (working set) memory has averaged at least 95% of its memory limit over the last 15 minutes and is still at least 95%. At 100% the kernel OOM-kills the container, which then shows up as restarts. The average is sample-weighted over the window. Only containers with a memory limit report `container/memory/limit_utilization`, so containers without a limit never fire. Uses GKE system metrics, so it covers every cluster and system namespaces. The working set includes some reclaimable page cache, so cache-heavy workloads can sit in the 90s without OOM kills: tune the threshold, or exclude namespaces in the query. Containers that stopped reporting more than 5 minutes before their cluster's newest sample are ignored.

query.base:
SET unmapped_fields = "nullify";
TS metrics-gcp.gke.otel-*
| WHERE resource.attributes.gcp.resource_type == "k8s_container"
    // Non-evictable memory is the working set the OOM killer acts on
    AND attributes.memory_type == "non-evictable"
// Per container and minute: limit utilization sample sum and count (for a sample-weighted mean) and the latest value.
// limit_utilization is only emitted for containers with a memory limit; used_bytes is emitted for every container.
| STATS utilization_sum = SUM(SUM_OVER_TIME(`metrics.kubernetes.io/container/memory/limit_utilization`)),
        utilization_samples = SUM(COUNT_OVER_TIME(`metrics.kubernetes.io/container/memory/limit_utilization`)),
        utilization_last = MAX(LAST_OVER_TIME(`metrics.kubernetes.io/container/memory/limit_utilization`)),
        used_samples = SUM(COUNT_OVER_TIME(`metrics.kubernetes.io/container/memory/used_bytes`))
    BY resource.attributes.project_id, resource.attributes.location, resource.attributes.cluster_name,
       resource.attributes.namespace_name, resource.attributes.pod_name, resource.attributes.container_name,
       bucket = TBUCKET(1 minute)
// Newest memory sample of each cluster, for the per-cluster freshness rule. Containers without a limit count, so a
// deleted limited container can't stay the newest; limit_utilization can arrive minutes after used_bytes.
| EVAL sampled = CASE(used_samples > 0 OR utilization_samples > 0, bucket)
| INLINE STATS cluster_newest = MAX(sampled)
    BY resource.attributes.project_id, resource.attributes.location, resource.attributes.cluster_name
| STATS utilization_sum = SUM(utilization_sum),
        utilization_samples = SUM(utilization_samples),
        latest_utilization = LAST(utilization_last, bucket) WHERE utilization_samples > 0,
        last_seen = MAX(sampled),
        cluster_newest = MAX(cluster_newest)
    BY resource.attributes.project_id, resource.attributes.location, resource.attributes.cluster_name,
       resource.attributes.namespace_name, resource.attributes.pod_name, resource.attributes.container_name

data.content:
## Container memory near limit

The container's non-evictable memory has stayed at or above 95% of its memory limit for the window (`avg_utilization`) and still is (`latest_utilization`).

### Triage
1. Open **[GCP OTel] GKE Pod Detail** for the pod. **Memory used by container** shows the trend against the request and limit: a steady climb suggests a leak, a flat line at the limit suggests an undersized limit or a cache that fills whatever it gets.
2. Check **Restarts over time** on the same dashboard. Restarts with memory at the limit are the evidence of OOM kills; OOM reasons aren't in this data.
3. Use **[GCP OTel] GKE Cluster Detail** to see whether other replicas of the workload behave the same way.

### Remediation
- Raise the container's memory limit (and request) if the working set is legitimately larger.
- Fix leaks, or cap runtime heaps and caches (for example JVM `-Xmx` or `MaxRAMPercentage`) below the limit.

### Notes
- Non-evictable memory is the working-set equivalent; it includes active page cache, which the kernel can reclaim under pressure before killing.
- Raise or lower the 0.95 threshold in both conditions of the last `WHERE`. To exclude namespaces, add `AND resource.attributes.namespace_name NOT IN (...)` to the first `WHERE`.
